summary: Arthur Venis (1857–1918) was an Indologist educated at the University of Edinburgh and Balliol College, Oxford (B.A. ~1874–1878). He served as professor and principal at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (1881–1888) and taught post-Vedic Sanskrit at the University of Allahabad (~1914–1918).

Arthur W. Ryder (1877–1938) was an Indologist who studied at Harvard, Berlin, and Leipzig (Ph.D. 1901) under Charles Rockwell Lanman and Karl Friedrich Geldner. He served as Instructor in Sanskrit at Harvard (1902–1906) and professor at UC Berkeley.

Arthur Waley (1889–1966) worked in sinology, japanology, and Buddhist studies, studying at King's College, Cambridge, and under Gustav Haloun, Laurence Binyon, and Hidetsugu Yagi. He served at the British Museum (1913–1929) and SOAS (1948).
Arthur Woollgar Verrall (1851–1912) was an academic who studied at Wellington College (~1865–1869) and Trinity College, Cambridge (~1869–1873). He later taught Robert Alexander Neil.
Aruna Haldar (b. 1918) is a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied under Kedarnath Ojha and Girindrasekhar Bose. She held a teaching post at Patna University.

Arunoday Natvarlal Jani (1921–2003) was an Indologist who completed his Ph.D. at the University of Mumbai (1953) under G. H. Bhatt. He served as professor and Sanskrit department head at Baroda and directed the Oriental Institute, Vadodara (1975–1981).

Arvind Sharma (b. 1940) is an Indologist, philosopher, and religious studies scholar educated at Allahabad, Syracuse, and Harvard. He held posts at the University of Queensland (1976–1980), University of Sydney (1980), and McGill University as Birks Chair (1994).

Aryadeva (200–250) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Nagarjuna and Shakyamitra. He was a colleague at the Mithila Institute of Post-Graduate Studies and Research in Sanskrit Learning and taught Candrakīrti, Tilopa, and Shakyamitra, among others.

Asanga Tilakaratne (b. 1952) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. At the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies, University of Kelaniya, he served as Head of Buddhist Thought (attested 1993) and Professor and Head of Buddhist Philosophy.

Asatoshi Kamiya is a scholar in Buddhist studies who earned an M.A. from Komazawa University (attested 1973). Kamiya held a teaching post at Mejiro Kenshin Junior and Senior High School (attested 1978).

Asef Bayat (b. 1954) studied at the University of Tehran and University of Kent (Ph.D. 1978–1984). He held posts at the American University in Cairo, Leiden University (2003–2010), and the Catherine and Bruce Bastian Chair at UIUC (~2010).

Asen Balikci (1929–2019) earned a PhD from Columbia University (1956). He held positions at the Musée d'ethnographie de Neuchâtel (~1953–1954), the National Museum of Canada (~1957–1968), and was professor of ethnology at the Université de Montréal (1963–1993).

Ashby Butnor is a philosopher who completed a Ph.D. at the University of Hawaiʻi in 2009 under Graham Parkes and Vrinda Dalmiya. She served as a visiting assistant professor at Metropolitan State University of Denver (attested 2011).

Ashok Aklujkar (b. 1941) works in Indology, linguistics, and philosophy. He studied at Savitribai Phule Pune University and Harvard (Ph.D. ~1965–1970) under Daniel H. H. Ingalls, and served in Asian Studies at the University of British Columbia (1969–2006).

Ashok Gangadean (b. 1947) is a philosopher who completed his Ph.D. at Brandeis University. In 1981, he became the Margaret Gest Professor of Global Philosophy at Haverford College, and he also founded the Global Dialogue Institute.

Ashok Kumar Chatterjee (1925–2021) was an Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies scholar who earned degrees including a Ph.D. at Banaras Hindu University under T. R. V. Murti. He taught at Dr. Bhimrao Ambedkar University (1950–1963) and BHU (1963–1985).

Ashutosh Mukherjee (1864–1924) studied at Presidency College and the University of Calcutta (B.A. ~1880–1883). He served at the Calcutta High Court (1904), was Tagore Professor of Law at Calcutta (1906–1914), and served as president of The Asiatic Society (~1907–1915).

Asim Kumar Chatterjee (b. 1940) is an Indology and history scholar who earned a Ph.D. from the University of Calcutta (1967) under D. Mukherjee. He served as a senior research fellow at Calcutta and lectured at Jangipur College.

Asko Parpola (b. 1941) is an Indologist and linguist who studied under Pentti Aalto, R. Panneerselvam, and P. R. Subramanian. He held posts at the Nordic Institute of Asian Studies and served as professor at the University of Helsinki (~1982–2004).

Astley John Hilary Goodwin (1900–1959) was an archaeologist who studied at St. John's College, Selwyn College (1919–1922), and SOAS University of London (1922). He took up a post at the University of Cape Town in 1923.
